patent_grounding.rationale: The revision 3 components and principal descriptions are directly grounded in the cited detailed description and claims. It correctly separates bridge mounting on the nut barrel from the connecting-groove passage, and preserves dependent-claim qualification for ball diameter and groove depth. The background rotation-to-translation action is separately cited as general ball-screw operation, not presented as a claim limitation.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model covers the disclosed shaft, mating nut, rolling balls, bridge members, opposed-groove passage, bridge connecting grooves, ball circulation, and claim 1–3 geometry. Excluding an actuator architecture and other surrounding equipment is appropriately cautious.

flow_consistency.rationale: Revision 3 adds a nut-to-bridge circulation interface using compatible mechanical_motion ports and the ball_circulation flow, while retaining the separate fitted_contact mounting interface. Alongside the balls-to-bridge rolling-passage interface and the shaft/nut-to-ball groove contact interfaces, this represents the disclosed relationship: balls roll in the opposed shaft/nut grooves and circulate through bridge grooves that connect nut grooves. The patent does not specify a directional sequence, so inout ports and no asserted direction are reasonable.

claim_traceability.rationale: The contact-angle and dependent dimensional parameters are represented with claim-linked citations and the dependent status is explicit in the latter two requirement statements. The circulation action is cited to the detailed description; the rotation/translation action is cited to background text.

interfaces.rationale: Interfaces reference existing subsystems, ports, and flows with compatible mechanical_contact or mechanical_motion types. The nut-bridge fitted mounting connection remains distinct from the nut-groove/bridge-connecting-groove circulation-passage connection. Recording the mating interfaces once on the nut subsystem is consistent with the supplied SJS convention.

textbook_application.rationale: The physical decomposition uses actual components, and surrounding actuator/drive details are not fabricated where the patent leaves them unspecified. Textbook guidance is used only to support cautious modeling choices, not as evidence for invention facts.

summary: Independent review of saved revision 3: the previously missing bridge connecting-groove to nut screw-groove connection is now represented as a distinct circulation-passage interface, separate from bridge mounting contact. Together with the ball-to-bridge circulation connection and the ball contacts with opposed shaft/nut grooves, the SJS expresses the supported route without inventing a direction. The modeled components, actions, claims, and interfaces are adequately patent-grounded; no unresolved findings identified.
